comments.author: @tysoncung
comments.text: The part that surprised me most was not that China leads, but how completely Europe left. Until the mid twentieth century European yards built most of the world's ships; today the continent mostly builds cruise liners, while China, South Korea and Japan turn out roughly nine tenths of merchant tonnage between them, with Korea taking the hardest jobs like gas carriers. Sources are listed in the description if you want to check the figures. Is there a shipyard or a dock near you, and is it still working?
